result.summary: Тесты после доработки стали крепче: все 154 теста зелёные 6 раз подряд, замечания первого прохода закрыты (мои 33 мутанта по ним и все 42 мутанта из проекта убиты). Шаг всё же не проходит (пункт 3 роли): из 189 моих новых мутантов 57 выжили, и среди них 9, которые заставляют проверку прекратить поиск после первого безобидного места в файле (сертификат, адрес-заглушка, шаблонный Bearer, пара с выражением, JWT из двух частей) и пропустить настоящий секрет дальше в том же файле, - ни один тест этого не замечает. Кроме того, замкнутые списки требования (25 из 26 слов-типов, 4 из 5 знаков начала блока и др.) проверены одним образцом, а прибор критерия 7 даёт ложный красный при двукратной перегрузке процессора (до 1,5 раза зелёный).

findings.where: tools/test/team-result-bytes.test.js: POSITIONS and RB-06 (criterion 3), RB-07, RB-08 PAIRS; role item 3 (do the tests catch an error)
findings.what: No test puts a REAL secret after a KEPT item of the same form in one file, so a scan that stops (or skips ahead) after the first kept item is not seen. 9 mutants of mine that make findSecrets miss a later secret survived all seven files (bytes file + six guard files, 140 tests, 0 red): u3 findPem returns false after the first certificate header (a certificate followed by a private key, the usual PEM bundle, is stored); u4 findUrlPassword returns false after the first kept address (a placeholder address, then an address with a real password, is stored); u5 findBearer returns false after the first kept Bearer (a template, then a literal); u6 findNamedValue returns null after the first kept pair (token: data.token, then password=<literal>); u7 findJwt returns false after the first non-JWT eyJ run (a two-part run, then a real three-part JWT); u8, u9, u10 (the same loops skip 200 or 60 characters after a kept item); n2 findPem skips 40 characters after a certificate line. I checked by direct calls that each mutant really returns null where the real code returns F1/F3/F8/F9/F7 (e.g. cert + private key, kept address + address with a password, Bearer template + Bearer abc1234, kept pair + password=hunter2fake, two-part + three-part JWT). The refused samples are placed alone, in the middle of 1 MiB of plain text, and beside O1-O3 only; O1-O3 hold no pair, address, Bearer or certificate, so the position never has a kept item of the form in front of the secret. The timing file does not help (its inputs hold no secret except the bait at the very end, after repeated kept units of ONE form, and the bait is of the prefix-key form).
findings.fix: Add a fourth position to POSITIONS (and use it in RB-06 and RB-11): 'after the whole assembly O10, and again after it' - O10 holds a kept sample of every form (certificate, addresses with placeholders, Bearer/Authorization templates, expression pairs, a two-part eyJ run), so one position kills u3-u10 and n2; expected side unchanged (refused). Also add 5-6 explicit pairs to PAIRS/RB-08 with the kept item first and the secret second (and the reverse order), one per form F1, F3, F7, F8, F9, F2. I ran these on the real code and they are refused: a certificate block followed by a private-key header; a placeholder address then an address with a literal password; 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' then 'Bearer abc1234'; 'token: data.token' then 'password=hunter2fake'; a two-part eyJ run then the three-part JWT of C6.

findings.where: tools/test/team-result-timing.test.js (the instrument of criterion 7); role item 6 (series under load, AP-115)
findings.what: The instrument gives a FALSE red when the processor is oversubscribed. On this machine (10 cores) I ran the timing file alone while N busy loops ran: N=1: 14/14 green (94.5 s); N=5: 14/14 (108.3 s); N=10: 14/14 (126.7 s); N=15: 14/14 (122.1 s); N=20: 12/14, red = family 2 (ratio 12.83) and family 10 (9.49), message 'size 1: the time grows by a factor of ... (limit 8), 4 of n repeats'; N=24: 11/14, red = family 1 (ratio 11.24), family 11 (9.35), family 10 (10.79). The code under test is linear in all these runs. Cause: the wall clock (process.hrtime) of a short 256 KiB measurement of about 20-40 ms is mostly one scheduler slice, the 1 MiB measurement spans several slices, so under time slicing the ratio inflates up to the oversubscription factor (4 x 2.4 > 8); the requirement fixes the clock (hrtime), the test follows it. The quiet-machine margin is wide (measured ratios 3.2-4.2 against the limit 8; the quadratic control 226 against 64; one call of the quadratic control on 128 KiB takes 11.5 s). A moderate load (a series of the 8 files together, five times, and timing next to the bytes file) never failed. The first report found no red at 10 and 20 loops; on this 10-core machine the limit is between 15 and 20.
findings.fix: Not blocking. If ORCH wants robustness: measure CPU time (process.cpuUsage) instead of the wall clock, or repeat a failed size once before the verdict; both need a one-line amendment of criterion 7 (it names process.hrtime.bigint). TEST-RUNNER: if the timing file is red with a ratio between 8 and 20 while other work runs, rerun it alone and attach both outputs (quality-bar 6 item 4).
